candidates.title: [Bug]: expression-bodied function result is not checked against the declared return type (Go interface-conversion crash)
candidates.body:
### Description
An expression-bodied function (`=> E`) is not type-checked against its declared return type. The program compiles, and the wrongly typed value then crashes the interpreter with a Go runtime error (`interface conversion: values.BalValue is int64, not string`).

This affects module-level functions, methods, and anonymous functions with an explicit signature. The only form that is checked is an anonymous function with inferred parameter types (`function (int) returns string f = x => x;` is correctly rejected). The equivalent block-body form `{ return x; }` is correctly rejected with `incompatible type: expected string, got int`.

### Steps to Reproduce
Runtime crash:
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

function g(int x) returns string => x;

public function main() {
    string s = g(3);
    io:println(s);
    io:println(s.length());
}
```
Actual (`bal run`):
```
3
error: interface conversion: values.BalValue is int64, not string
        at main(ae.bal:8)
```
Expected: a compile error at line 3 (`function g(int x) returns string => x;`): incompatible type, expected `string`, got `int`.

Compile-time checks missing on every marked line (this compiles and exits 0):
```ballerina
function strAsInt() returns int => "hello"; // @error

function intAsString(int x) returns string => x; // @error

class C {
    function m(int x) returns string => x; // @error
}

public function main() {
    var f = function (int x) returns string => x; // @error
    _ = f;
}
```
`function strAsInt() returns int => "hello";` also compiles, and calling it returns a string.

Spec, [§7.3.3 Expression-bodied functions](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#expr-function-body): "An expr-function-body of the form `=> E` is short for a block-function-body `{ return E}`." So each `=> E` body must be checked like `return E`, which the return statement requires to be a subtype of the declared return type.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ 222c3007635fe096bbf771d3e79d5a39754214e5

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go 1.27.1, `go run ./cli/cmd run <file>`

### Related area
Type checker

### Related issue(s) (optional)
#1122 (closed, anonymous function vs. expected function type) is different: it is about the function type, not about checking the body against its own return type.

notes: Hit the 5-candidate limit, so the run stopped early (about 20 minutes of wall-clock time). The spec was fetched from ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/ without problems. About 30 other reproducible deviations were dropped as duplicates of open issues, including #1169, #1046, #1454, #1047, #1392, #1044, #1511, #1347, #1132, #1091, #1374, #1214, #1026, #1452, #1043, #1223, #1253, #1050, #1564, #1166, #1217, #1250, #1076, #1559, #1116 and #1520. Other candidates were dropped or left out: decimal:round(1.5d, 34) panicking (spec ambiguous; the corpus deliberately expects a panic) and toString control-character escapes like \x01 (UNCERTAIN; a partial overlap with #1387). A possible comment on #1250 was cut to stay within the limit: a non-const annotation value keeps aliasing a mutable module list, so arr.push is visible through T.@a. Corpus test corpus/bal/subset9/09-value/fromjsonwithtype-negative-v.bal deliberately encodes the cloneWithType-defaults gap (#1026). subset10.md contradicts itself on `readonly` class qualifiers (line 23 vs line 347). Possible new leads not run through the pipeline: in an isolated function, `new` of a class with no init where a field initializer reads mutable module state is accepted (inverse of #1076; #1657 may cover it), and adding members to a list or map during foreach does not panic (spec 5.8.2).
